prior_importants.description: A rescope that lands while `pup fix` is starting a round on a merged session is lost. That round runs under hooks compiled from the old scope, and `recordSessionRoute` then writes its standard route back over the critical tier the rescope just set.

A rescope of a blocked session (or of an awaiting-review one the gate then parks) never reaches the worker's hooks. The only way to resume it, `pup unblock` then `pup kill --respawn`, relaunches from the launch-time compiled settings.json, scope-in.pat and context.md. Edits to the newly added globs stay BLOCKED even though the rescope reported success.

findings.description: `listProcesses` finds `ps` on `PROBE_PATH`, which lists `/opt/homebrew/bin` and `/usr/local/bin` before `/usr/bin` and `/bin`, and the operator's uid can write both. The conductor can plant a `ps` there that prints nothing. `launchedAncestor()` then finds no ancestor, and `env -u PUP_CONDUCTOR pup plan edit … --rescope` from the conductor's own Bash succeeds and is recorded as the inferred operator, which is the very case ADR 0115 says is refused.
findings.body:
**The problem.** The process-tree check is the one refusal ADR 0115 says a worker cannot shed: "So `env -u PUP_CONDUCTOR pup plan edit ... --rescope` from the conductor's own Bash is refused". But it trusts whatever `ps` comes first on `PROBE_PATH`, and that PATH starts with two directories the operator's user can write:

```ts
export const PROBE_PATH = [
  '/opt/homebrew/bin',
  '/usr/local/bin',
  '/usr/bin',
  '/bin',
  ...
```
https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/526406a3c4c28a6242634b76f205350310858001/src/claude/session-runtime.service.ts#L1016-L1025

The repo itself says `/opt/homebrew/bin` "is group-writable on a standard install" (`src/core/sandbox-profile.utils.ts:123`). The conductor runs as that same uid.

**Trigger.**
1. From the conductor's Bash, write `/opt/homebrew/bin/ps` as a script that exits 0 and prints nothing. It could also exec `/bin/ps` and drop the lines containing `--name pup-`.
2. Run `env -u PUP_CONDUCTOR pup plan edit <task> --rescope --scope <glob>` on a task whose session is `awaiting-review` or `merged` with its window closed.

**What goes wrong.**
- `listProcesses` returns `undefined` only when `execFileSync` throws. Output that exits cleanly becomes a table, even an empty one (https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/526406a3c4c28a6242634b76f205350310858001/src/claude/session-runtime.service.ts#L1139-L1157).
- `launchedAncestor` finds nothing in that table and returns `undefined` (https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/526406a3c4c28a6242634b76f205350310858001/src/core/task-rescope.service.ts#L192-L205).
- `rescopeOrRefuse` refuses only on `'launched'` or `'unreadable'`, so the rescope goes through (`src/cli/index.ts` L881-902).
- `callingConductor()` reads only `PUP_CONDUCTOR`, and the window probe never looks at the conductor's own window, so nothing else refuses it.
- The event and the decision record then name `inferred-operator`, so the audit trail credits the operator with a scope widening the conductor made.

**Why this is not one of ADR 0115's accepted limits.** The ADR accepts a writable prefix only for tmux, which really does install under Homebrew ("One that can write one of those directories can still replace the tmux there … that is a ceiling like the socket one"). `ps` always ships with the OS, so nothing needs to look for it in a package manager's prefix. The tree check's only accepted escape is a process that left the tree, and here the conductor never leaves it.

**Possible fix.** Look `ps` up on a separate root-owned path: `/bin:/usr/bin`, plus `/run/current-system/sw/bin` so NixOS, which has no `/bin/ps`, keeps working. Leave `PROBE_PATH` as it is for tmux. Checking that the table holds `process.ppid` is a reasonable extra check, but it is not enough alone: a wrapper around the real `ps` that drops lines passes it. If you would rather accept the risk, the ADR's ceiling sentence should name `ps` as well as tmux.

process_issues.description: Round 5 budget: spawned only correctness (2 instances), security (2 instances) and guards. Skipped conventions, docs, context, simplicity and maintainability under the round budget. Skipped workflow-safety because no `.github/workflows` file changed, and spec because there is no closing issue or spec source.
Not spawned: the reviewers returned a single finding, so there was nothing to group and dedup was trivial.

Prior important on session.repository.ts 348-355 is marked unresolved. 526406a removed `blocked` from RESCOPABLE_STATES, which closes the direct case. The parenthetical path is still reachable at head, as correctness instance 1 verified. An awaiting-review session is rescoped with its window closed, its re-gate rejects, and `rejectOrBlock` parks it as blocked because re-steering needs a window. `pup unblock` and `pup kill --respawn` then go through `relaunchWindow`, which launches from the launch-time compiled settings.json, scope-in.pat and context.md.
